The Doolittles were among the founders of Wallingford, Connecticut, in 1670, and they stayed in the hills north of
New Haven for four generations, at Wallingford and then at Mount Carmel in Hamden.
After the Revolution, like so many Connecticut families, they went west in steps.
All but one of Titus Doolittle's children left Connecticut.
His son Benjamin, a ship carpenter, settled first near the Catskills, where Luther was born in Greene County in 1804,
and then moved on to Newfield, near the head of Cayuga Lake.
The Finger Lakes had been Iroquois country until the war; afterwards New York surveyed much of it into soldiers' bounty
lands and sold the rest, and New Englanders poured in.
The Doolittles stayed in the lake country for three generations.
Horace tried the West in the 1850s: his son William Homer was born in Michigan,
and in 1860 the family was farming in Buchanan County, Iowa.
They were back at Newfield by 1864, when Horace went to the war with the 179th New York.
William Homer became a miller at Genoa, on the east shore of Cayuga Lake, where Esther was born in 1890.
In 1908 she married William H. Snyder in Syracuse, and the Connecticut line met the Lorraine one.
